record.notes: Presented in the Senate on 11 February 2026 by Sen. Karina Isabel Ruiz Ruiz (Morena) and referred to the joint committees on Legislative Studies and on the Analysis, Monitoring and Evaluation of AI in Mexico; published in the Gaceta del Senado of 11 February 2026 (LXVI Legislature, second year).

verification.note: CAUTION: the title, date and status rest on a secondary source. Stored: a legislative alert by the law firm Basham (26 February 2026, in English), which describes the initiative presented on 11 February 2026 by Sen. Karina Isabel Ruíz Ruíz, its referral to the joint committees and its content (regulatory agency, risk classification, provider obligations, prohibitions, deepfakes, sanctions); the summary rests on that alert. The alert links the Senate gazette PDF of the initiative (file 'Ini_Morena_Sen_Karina_Ruiz_Expide_Ley_Nacional_de_Inteligencia_Artificial.pdf'), which is not yet stored, so original_title and the Spanish wording of the bill are not confirmed by a stored copy. The alert calls the bill the National Law to Regulate the Use of Artificial Intelligence, while the gazette file name has 'Expide Ley Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial'; the gazette wording is used. The Secretaría de Gobernación's SIL tracking report (official_url) was read on 12 October 2026 and gave the status 'pendiente en comisión(es) de origen', but could not be stored because its TLS certificate could not be verified. Not confirmed by any stored copy: that the bill is one of several dozen AI bills pending in Congress and that no general federal AI law had been adopted by October 2026; and press reports of a separate draft 'Ley General para Regular y Fomentar la Inteligencia Artificial' prepared by the Senate AI commission (223 articles, not voted by the close of the April 2026 session, said to depend on a reform of constitutional articles 3 and 73), which is not recorded separately. No committee action on this initiative appears in the stored copy.
